newsitem.title: USA: UNDERWRITERS REINSURANCE RATINGS AFFIRMED - S&P.
newsitem.headline: UNDERWRITERS REINSURANCE RATINGS AFFIRMED - S&P.

text.p: NEW YORK, June 24 - Standard & Poor's today has affirmed its double-'A'-minus claims-paying ability and issuer credit ratings on Underwriters Reinsurance Co. and its single-'A'-minus senior debt and issuer credit ratings on URC Holdings Corp.
The ratings are based on the following:

-- Underwriters Re is among the top ten domestic reinsurers based on statutory capital and continues to be a major beneficiary of the flight-to-quality due to its reputation for prudent risk selection and overall capital adequacy. Recent capital infusions from parent Alleghany Corp. have also allowed Underwriters Re to increase lines on quality accounts and to underwrite a wider spectrum of risks.
-- Underwriters Re has exhibited strong operating performance during the past five years and generally outperformed industry averages for both underwriting and profitability measures.
In addition, financial returns have begun to rebound due to improving portfolio yields on a growing invested asset base.

-- Management is committed to disciplined underwriting, as Underwriters Re is focused on maintaining sufficient risk-adjusted returns. The company has proven its ability to respond opportunistically to changing market conditions, while maintaining meaningful treaty participations with many of its clients to justify the expenses of detailed underwriting and actuarial analysis of each piece of business.

-- Capital contributions from both the proceeds of the URC Holdings senior debt offering and parent Alleghany have added $271 million since 1993 to statutory surplus, which stood at $592 million at March 31, 1997. Underwriters Re's capital adequacy ratio is superior at 293% and is expected to remain at or above the double-'A' level for the foreseeable future.

-- Although pre-1986 liabilities are a source of some continuing earnings drag, the relatively low market share of Underwriters Re during the years before the pollution exclusion clause puts a reasonable upper bound on exposures.
A sizable percentage of current mass action reserves represent bulk and incurred-but-not-reported reserves.

The 1996 combined ratio of 102.3% was in line with Standard & Poor's expectation for the year. Going forward, Standard & Poor's expects underwriting results to continue to outperform the industry average due to tight underwriting controls and a particularly expense efficient organization. Standard & Poor's also expects continued incurred loss development of 2-3 loss ratio points over the next few years. Investment returns are expected to improve due to enhanced yields on higher levels of invested assets.

Standard & Poor's believes that Underwriters Re's pretax operating income for 1997 should approach the $45 million mark, thus generating a return on revenue in the 10% range, which is commensurate with the rating category given the conservative four year duration of the company's fixed income portfolio.
